chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Isa or someone else, from Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad ibn Zakariyya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Vegetables were mentioned in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), so he said: 'Eat the leek, for its example among the vegetables is like the example of bread among the rest of the food,' or he said: 'Among the sauces.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of leeks in Shia hadith and how did the Prophet describe them?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the leek (*al-kurrath*) to a staple status, comparing its essential role among vegetables to that of bread among all foods or *idam* (savory accompaniments). This comparison underscores the leek's historical significance in the Prophetic diet not merely as a vegetable, but as a fundamental source of sustenance and health, reflecting the Shia emphasis on practical medical wisdom (*tibb*) derived from the Ahl al-Bayt. The narration highlights the holistic Islamic view of food, where dietary choices are intertwined with physical well-being and spiritual discipline.
